Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) provide access to these components in human genetic backgrounds. This review follows the development of ALS models from motor neuron cultures to neuromuscular cocultures, engineered tissues, and organoids, and compares the biological conclusions their experiments support. Genotype-specific analyses distinguish intervention-supported mechanisms from candidate links to axonal maintenance, junctional organization, and muscle output. Comparisons of a shared SOD1 G85R variant and riluzole responses show how genetic design, cellular state, stimulation, and endpoint definitions determine interpretation. The reviewed neuromuscular systems provide experimentally modifiable structural and contraction phenotypes. Their clinical predictive advantage over motor neuron cultures remains unestablished because the necessary paired assay comparisons and independent clinical validation are missing from these studies. Model selection should follow the question being tested, including neuronal injury, cellular contribution, transmission failure, or loss of established function. Reproducible measurements, patient stratification, aging assessment, and integration with clinical data, complementary cellular approaches, animal experiments, and computational analysis provide routes to resolving the identified evidence gaps.

title: Melatonin and GABA Improve Metabolic and Pancreatic Outcomes in Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetic Mice with Selective Benefits of Combination Therapy.
abstract: Loss of functional β-cell mass is a critical factor in the pathogenesis of type 1 (T1D) and type 2 (T2D) diabetes, both characterized by chronic hyperglycemia. Melatonin (M) and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA; G) exhibit immunoregulatory properties and have shown potential to preserve or restore β-cell mass in experimental diabetic models. Thus, we aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of melatonin and GABA, alone and in combination (M+G), on β-cell regeneration and metabolic regulation in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced T1D and high-fat diet (HFD)-induced T2D mouse models. BALB/c mice received STZ (50 mg/kg/day) for five consecutive days to induce T1D, while C57BL/6J mice were fed an HFD for 30 weeks to induce insulin resistance and T2D. Both models were subsequently treated with M, G, or M+G for six weeks. In T1D mice, both monotherapies and combination therapy reduced fasting blood glucose levels, increased plasma insulin levels, improved glucose tolerance, promoted β-cell proliferation and transdifferentiation, and reduced β-cell apoptosis. In T2D mice, treatments improved metabolic parameters and glycolipid metabolism in the liver and adipose tissue, respectively, skeletal muscle mitochondrial function, peripheral insulin sensitivity and β-cell mass. Overall, M and G monotherapies demonstrated beneficial metabolic and β-cell protective effects in both models. However, combination therapy provided additional benefits for only selected endpoints, with most direct comparisons showing no significant differences and most significant melatonin × GABA interactions being consistent with sub-additive effects.

title: Multi-Modal Programmed Cell Death and Immune Microenvironment Alterations Associated with Ligamentum Flavum Hypertrophy and Ossification: An Integrative Bioinformatic Analysis with Single-Cell and m6A Profiling.
abstract: Hypertrophy and ossification of the ligamentum flavum cause spinal stenosis and myelopathy, yet the roles of programmed cell death (PCD) and immune remodeling remain unclear. We profiled five PCD modalities, immune infiltration, and m6A regulators in ligamentum flavum bulk transcriptomes (GSE113212; n = 8), with validation in GSE206560 (N6-methyladenosine (m6A) MeRIP-seq) and GSE106253, and single-cell analysis of GSE294458/GSE267819 (33,817 cells) replicated in GSE271018 (51,686 cells). Ferroptosis showed the largest direction-consistent score difference (GSVA p = 0.029; GSEA NES = 1.60) and correlated with macrophage infiltration (r = 0.859, p = 0.006) and immune-checkpoint expression. Single-cell analysis localized ferroptosis activity to SPP1+ macrophages in two independent cohorts; SPP1 signaling was predicted to originate from this subset and target fibroblasts via SPP1-CD44 and SPP1-integrin pairs; macrophage ferroptosis activity increased along a computational state ordering (ρ = 0.354). More m6A peaks were detected in ossified libraries (15,102 vs. 6073 sites), with hypermethylation and downregulation of SLC7A11 (logFC = -2.81, adj. p = 0.008). A six-gene signature (five genes detectable in the external cohorts) separated disease from control samples in three cohorts (internal AUC = 1.0, exploratory). These convergent associations nominate an m6A-SLC7A11-ferroptosis-SPP1+ macrophage axis as a candidate, hypothesis-generating mechanism requiring experimental validation.

title: Gangliosides and Other Glycolipids as Multiple Players in the Nervous System: Their Implications for Human Disorders.
abstract: Gangliosides, including GM1 ganglioside (GM1), are sialic acid-containing glycosphingolipids that are involved in essential physiological roles such as cell-cell recognition, adhesion, transmembrane signaling, neuronal development, and cell fate determination. They are crucial to all phases of neuronal development. Gangliosides are enriched in the outer layer of neuronal membranes of the nervous system, where their contents are ten times higher than in other cell types. Moreover, gangliosides (especially GM1) have neuroprotective effects on neuronal cells through various pathways, although the identities of these pathways remain relatively unclear. Notably, some neurodegenerative diseases, such as Parkinson's disease, have recently been reported to be associated with significant deficiencies of some gangliosides. Because of their location on the outer layer of the plasma membrane of neurons and immune cells, some anti-ganglioside antibodies can attack and bind to these cell-surface gangliosides. These antibodies provoke unexpected and unfavorable effects in neuronal and immune cells, as observed in Guillain-Barré syndrome with anti-GM1 antibodies. At present, however, the molecular mechanisms of these unfavorable effects remain to be explored. Here, I describe the molecular actions of gangliosides in the nervous system as both neuroprotective and neurotoxic agents.

title: Nebularine, a Natural Adenosine Analog, Modulates Cell Cycle Progression, Migration, and Survival in Breast Cancer Cells: Integrating In Vitro Findings with In Silico Transcriptomic Analysis.
abstract: Breast cancer remains a highly heterogeneous malignancy, accounting for nearly one-third of female cancers worldwide; thus, there is an urgent need for novel selective agents to overcome treatment resistance and systemic toxicities. We investigated the selective antiproliferative, antimigratory, and pro-apoptotic mechanisms of Nebularine (NEB), a natural purine nucleoside analog, across breast cancer cellular models by integrating phenotypic and transcriptional responses with structural binding dynamics and clinical prognostic correlations. Cell viability and selective indices (SIs) were evaluated in breast cancer (MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7) and non-malignant human mammary epithelial (MCF-12A) cells using MTT assays across a 0-200 μM concentration range. Cellular motility was assessed via two-dimensional wound healing assays. Cell cycle kinetics and apoptotic populations were quantified using Annexin V/PI flow cytometry. qRT-PCR was performed to profile key cell cycle (CCNA2, CDK1, CDK2, CDKN1A/p21, CDKN1B/p27, and TP53) and apoptotic (BAX, BCL2L1/Bcl-XL, CASP9, and CASP3) transcripts. Structural interactions were investigated using AutoDock Vina molecular docking models. Clinical transcript expression and prognostic relevance were evaluated using TCGA/GTEx datasets via GEPIA2 and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses. NEB exerted moderate, dose-dependent antiproliferative activity, displaying an estimated IC50 of ~100 μM in aggressive MDA-MB-231 cells and IC50 > 200 μM in MCF-7 cells (57.93% viability at 200 μM), while non-malignant MCF-12A cells retained 99.75% viability at 200 μM (IC50 > 200 μM), yielding an in vitro selectivity index (SI) > 2.0. NEB treatment impaired two-dimensional wound closure in breast cancer cells without compromising baseline non-malignant cellular motility. Flow cytometry demonstrated prominent S-phase entrapment (accumulating up to 53.23%) alongside significant execution of apoptotic cell death. Transcriptional profiling revealed profound downregulation of key replication drivers (CCNA2 and CDK1) in both cancer lines, alongside p53-independent CDKN1A (p21) upregulation in MCF-7 cells. In silico docking predicted thermodynamically favorable structural compatibility with CDK1, Casp9, Bcl-XL, and Cyclin A2 (ΔG = -6.5 to -6.6 kcal/mol). Clinically, CCNA2 and CDK1 were overexpressed in BRCA primary tumors (p < 0.05) and portended poor survival, whereas elevated CASP9 expression correlated with extended overall and progression-free survival (p < 0.05). NEB acts as a selective purine nucleoside analog that triggers S-phase cell cycle arrest and apoptotic cell death in breast cancer models while demonstrating favorable selectivity over non-tumorigenic mammary epithelium. By transcriptionally suppressing pathologically elevated clinical drivers (such as CCNA2 and CDK1), NEB provides a promising structural template for further preclinical translational development.

title: Astrocyte Developmental Timing in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Stage × Module Framework.
abstract: Astrocytes play essential roles in neural circuit assembly, stabilization, and refinement, yet their contributions to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) have largely been considered within static or disorder-specific frameworks. Converging evidence indicates that astrocytes acquire distinct functional capacities across development. Here, we organize these capacities into six functional modules-synaptogenic support, excitatory-inhibitory (E/I) homeostasis, metabolic coupling, neuromodulatory regulation, inflammatory threshold setting, and neurovascular stabilization-each representing a partially separable domain of astrocyte function with a distinct developmental trajectory. We integrate these modules across three major developmental windows-fetal, early postnatal, and adolescent-to propose a stage × module framework of astrocyte involvement in NDDs. A central premise of this framework is that neurodevelopmental vulnerability may arise not solely from astrocyte dysfunction per se, but from temporal mismatches between the maturation of astrocyte functional capacity and evolving circuit demand. During early postnatal development, the convergence of synaptogenic signaling and glutamate transporter maturation defines a vulnerability window in which perturbations may preferentially destabilize circuit assembly and contribute to social, sensory, and hyperexcitability phenotypes. During adolescence, continued astrocyte remodeling, particularly in association cortices, intersects with increasing neuromodulatory and metabolic demands and may influence attentional and executive stability. Different forms of temporal mismatch-including delayed maturation, premature stabilization, and excessive gain amplification-may therefore generate distinct phenotype clusters even when the underlying molecular perturbations overlap. We further conceptualize sex as a developmental modifier that can shift the timing, amplitude, or sensitivity of astrocyte module trajectories through hormonal, chromosomal, and immune-mediated mechanisms. This dynamic perspective accommodates heterogeneity across diagnostic categories while preserving mechanistic coherence and generates testable predictions regarding stage-specific molecular signatures, phenotypic consequences, and therapeutic responses. By reframing NDDs as stage-dependent disruptions of astrocyte functional modules and their alignment with circuit demand, the proposed framework suggests that therapeutic strategies should incorporate developmental timing alongside molecular specificity, providing a conceptual basis for stage-informed intervention and developmental neuroglial precision medicine.

title: Astrocyte State-Dependent Remodeling of Neuron-Glia Communication in C9ORF72-Associated Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
abstract: Astrocyte dysfunction is an important component of non-cell-autonomous pathology in C9ORF72-associated amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (C9-ALS), yet how distinct astrocyte states contribute to altered neuron-glia communication remains unclear. Building on a previously published human single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) dataset of C9-ALS and control cortices, we reanalyzed motor-cortex samples using Seurat for preprocessing and integration, gene-set scoring for astrocyte-state characterization, and CellChat for pathway- and ligand-receptor-level communication inference. Donor-level analyses assessed astrocyte-state-specific communication differences, and an independent motor-cortex cohort was used to examine the reproducibility of key findings. CD44-high astrocytes showed stronger reactive features, whereas HPSE2-high astrocytes exhibited higher homeostasis/support scores. Although the overall number of inferred interactions was largely preserved, pooled communication strength was lower in C9-ALS. Donor-level analysis supported greater relative attenuation of HPSE2-high than CD44-high astrocyte communication with excitatory neurons. Pooled analyses showed prominent reductions in glutamate-related and neuronal adhesion/support pathways, whereas several extracellular matrix/remodeling-associated signals were relatively increased. Several altered pathways also extended into oligodendrocyte-associated two-step communication motifs. The independent cohort reproduced the astrocyte-state transcriptional profiles, with directionally consistent but statistically nonsignificant communication changes. Collectively, these findings provide a cell-state-resolved map of altered neuron-glia communication in C9-ALS and identify candidate signaling networks for further mechanistic investigation.

title: Metabolite Composition of Stem and Root Extracts of 5-Year-Old Polyscias fruticosa (L.) Harms and Insights into Their Neuroprotective Properties Using Model Systems of Alzheimer's Disease and Neurodegeneration Induced by Toxicants.
abstract: Polyscias fruticosa (L.) Harms (P. fruticosa) is a nootropic plant traditionally used to enhance cognitive function; however, its neuroprotective potential and bioactive constituents remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we evaluated aqueous (A5) and ethanolic (E5) extracts from the stems and roots of 5-year-old P. fruticosa for neuroprotective activities in transgenic Drosophila melanogaster expressing human amyloid precursor protein (hAPP), and in a trimethyltin (TMT)-induced mouse model of neurodegeneration. Both extracts dose-dependently restored memory and locomotor deficits and extended the median lifespan of hAPP flies to 42-48 days (vs. 36 days in untreated controls), with E5 showing stronger antioxidant activity. In TMT-treated mice, these extracts enhanced both short- and long-term spatial memory and attenuated anxiety-like behaviors; both extracts also preserved hippocampal pyramidal neurons and increased the number of differentiating (DCX+) and mature (NeuN+) neurons in the dentate gyrus. LC-MS/MS profiling identified putative oleanolic acid and chlorogenic acid derivatives as abundant bioactive metabolites; these were particularly enriched in E5. These findings support the traditional nootropic use of P. fruticosa plant materials and identify ethanolic extracts of stems and roots as promising, cost-effective candidates for future preclinical research into treatments for Alzheimer's disease and toxicant-induced neurodegeneration.

title: Multi-Omics Reveals MYDGF Dysregulation Associated with Synapse-Related Molecular Changes in Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Myeloid-derived growth factor (MYDGF) is a secreted protein involved in tissue repair and cellular protection, but its expression and molecular associations in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. We analyzed public bulk, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets, complemented by immunohistochemical images and Western blots in an AD mouse model. Bulk analyses showed lower MYDGF expression in AD fusiform gyrus and prefrontal cortex, with no significant differences in the insula or anterior cingulate cortex. Single-nucleus analyses detected MYDGF transcripts in neuronal and non-neuronal populations. In excitatory-neuron pseudobulk analyses of AD donors, MYDGF expression was positively associated with SYP and SYNGR1 in the PCC, while GSEA identified positive enrichment of synaptic vesicle cycle, cholinergic synapse, and synaptic vesicle endocytosis gene sets in the FCX. Spatial analyses revealed regional variation in MYDGF detection and associations with energy metabolism and apoptosis-related signatures. MYDGF abundance was lower in AD dorsolateral prefrontal cortex samples in the primary human proteomic cohort. Mouse Western blots showed lower MYDGF signal alongside reduced PSD-95 and synaptophysin levels. These findings indicate MYDGF downregulation in selected AD brain regions and suggest potential links with synaptic alterations. Despite lacking direct functional validation, this study provides a foundation for investigating MYDGF's potential role in AD.

title: Hippocampal Neurotopography in 3D Models of Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Animal models have long dominated Alzheimer's disease (AD) research, yet they fail to recapitulate the complex structural and functional scenery of the human hippocampus. Evidence from animal studies reveals differential vulnerabilities in cornu ammonis regions, particularly CA1 and CA3. This perspective presents the concept of neurotopographic fidelity, which integrates the accurate replication of spatial, cellular, and functional characteristics of a 3D engineered hippocampal model. Emphasizing structural subdivision, cellular diversity, and synaptic connectivity, our proposed framework serves as a guide to a biologically relevant AD model. We also address the constructional complexity and propose a workflow diagram for validating 3D hippocampal AD organoids using clinical data within this integrated model. By resolving these challenges, our framework offers a proposal for developing next-generation translational models that reflect human-specific AD signatures.

title: Mammary and brain pharmacokinetics of licochalcone A after oral and intravenous administration: implications for breast cancer prevention and interception.
abstract: Licochalcone A (LicA), a prenylated chalcone from Glycyrrhiza inflata, shows promising anti-tumor activity in breast cancer models, but translation is limited by poor bioavailability and rapid systemic clearance. Oral delivery is the clinically favored route for long-term use of breast cancer prevention drugs in women at elevated risk of developing breast cancer. We report the first validated quantification of LicA in mammary tissue in a prevention context and the first characterization of brain distribution under intact blood-brain barrier (BBB) conditions for intercepting brain metastasis. Formulations spanning aqueous (F07), lipid-based (L05), surfactant-rich (L13) and co-solvent (L022, L024) systems were selected by solubility screening and simulated gastrointestinal re-dispersibility. Eight independent pharmacokinetic studies were conducted across two species. Plasma, mammary, brain, and liver were quantified. Subcutaneous L022 (80 mg/kg/day, 28 days) that suppressed tumor growth in mice, presented a trough plasma LicA of 68 ng/mL (IQR 35-105), below in vitro-effective thresholds. Oral L024 in mice was rapidly absorbed (Tmax 0.25-0.5 h, plasma Cmax 817 ng/mL) and achieved mammary (Cmax 1,093 ng/g), with tissue-to-plasma partitioning (Kp) > 1 by every metric at 100 mg/kg. Brain-to-plasma Kp remained 0.3-0.5 after oral dosing but exceeded 1 from 1 h after intravenous dosing, reaching 3.92 at 8 h, while brain Cmax rose from 378 to 9,925 ng/g. Dose-normalized plasma exposure was 37-fold lower after oral than intravenous administration and brain exposure fell almost proportionally, by 27.5-fold. We interpret this as indicating that limited oral brain exposure reflects pre-systemic loss rather than restricted BBB transfer, although transfer kinetics were not measured directly. In rats, F07 was constrained by low drug-loading, while L05 and L13 achieved higher loading and prolonged T1/2 but were only characterized in plasma. L13 was not tolerated intravenously in pre-study tolerability assessment, and L05 was not advanced on formulation-development grounds rather than on pharmacokinetic performance. L024 was tolerated by both routes and was the only formulation for which tissue distribution data. It was selected as the lead candidate for chronic evaluation on the basis of tissue distribution data and dual-route tolerability. L024s short half-life predicts a low once-daily steady-state trough, addressable by divided dosing.

title: Hybridization between ivabradine and MEL55A results in compounds with improved potency on HCN channel isoforms.
abstract: A new series of phenylalkylamines structurally related to zatebradine and ivabradine was designed and prepared with the aim to find compounds showing preference or selectivity for individual HCN channel isoforms. The new compounds are characterized by a different degree of conformational freedom, and by the presence of stereogenic centers in the region connecting the basic nitrogen to the veratrol moieties. Their effects were evaluated on h-current mediated by homomeric mHCN1, mHCN2 and hHCN4 channels expressed in HEK 293 cells. Selected compounds were also assessed for effects on pacemaking activity in cardiomyocytes derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and in zebrafish embryos. All new compounds reduced h-current mediated by mHCN1, mHCN2 and hHCN4 channels. The most interesting compounds, derived from hybridization between MEL55A and ivabradine, were (R)-1c and (S)-1c. (R)-1c preferentially inhibited mHCN2/hHCN4 relative to mHCN1, whereas (S)-1c was a more potent but relatively non-selective blocker. Both compounds reduced pacemaking activity in hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and zebrafish embryos, demonstrating functional activity in both cellular and whole-organism models.

title: Sparse EEG neurodynamics of hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes with personal euglycemic baseline adaptation.
abstract: Hypoglycemia alters cerebral electrophysiological activity, providing a physiological basis for EEG-based detection. However, translation toward subject-independent monitoring remains constrained by uncertain minimum input requirements, insufficiently characterized stability of sparse representations and their physiological associations, and inter-participant baseline variability. This study benchmarked 24 models spanning engineered-feature machine learning, feature-domain deep learning, and raw-waveform deep learning under leave-one-subject-out validation. Channel-Feature Sparsification was applied using a predefined performance-preservation criterion. Sparse representations were evaluated for selection stability, cross-paradigm concordance, and physiological association. Personal Euglycemic Baseline Adaptation (PEBA) was subsequently applied using a short personal euglycemic reference without participant-specific model retraining. LDA achieved the highest observed balanced accuracy within the engineered-feature paradigm, whereas Sinc-SSNET performed best in both deep-learning paradigms. Sparsification retained the F7 log-theta descriptor for LDA, the F7 channel row for feature-domain Sinc-SSNET, and two channels for raw-waveform Sinc-SSNET. F7 was retained across all three paradigms, and its log-theta descriptor increased during hypoglycemia in 30 of 34 participants (88.2%). PEBA improved balanced accuracy from 0.71 to 0.77 for LDA, from 0.68 to 0.83 for feature-domain Sinc-SSNET, and from 0.71 to 0.78 for raw-waveform Sinc-SSNET. Compared with the corresponding full-input models, reduced configurations decreased parameter counts by 88.51%-99.88%, parameter storage requirements by 87.20%-99.88%, and multiply-accumulate operations by 94.72%-99.91%. These findings demonstrate the preservation of hypoglycemia-related EEG information under a predefined sparsification criterion, while personal euglycemic normalization improves cross-participant discrimination. Physiological consistency and reduced computational requirements support further evaluation of compact EEG-based hypoglycemia detection. Independent cohorts, continuous glycemic-transition recordings, and native sparse EEG acquisition are required before prospective application.

title: Combined effects of concurrent motor imagery and high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on human motor performance and corticospinal excitability.
abstract: Combined therapeutic maneuvers may be more effective for improving motor dysfunction than single interventions. Although motor imagery (MI) and high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) each may enhance cortical excitability and/or motor performance, whether simultaneous application yields superior effects remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate behavioral and neurophysiological changes induced by HF-rTMS applied concurrently with MI. Participants underwent four modulation procedures in a crossover design: MI of a typing task alone, 5-Hz rTMS over the left primary motor cortex alone, concurrent MI with 5 Hz rTMS, and a control condition. Before and after each intervention, motor performance was evaluated by means of actual and imagined movement time, error rate, MI vividness, and surface electromyography of intrinsic and extrinsic hand muscles. Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) elicited by single-pulse TMS were also recorded at rest, during MI, and actual movement. No significant changes in motor or MI performance were observed following any intervention. Task-related corticospinal excitability, expressed relative to resting MEP amplitude (%rest), decreased during actual movement after concurrent MI with HF-rTMS compared with the control and MI-alone conditions. MEP persistence in the agonist muscle remained stable during HF-rTMS alone but declined during the latter half of the combined MI and HF-rTMS intervention. These findings suggest that concurrent MI and HF-rTMS modulated task-related corticospinal excitability without measurable changes in motor performance. This combination may enhance the modulation of motor cortical output in a task-dependent manner, supporting a neuromodulatory framework for optimizing motor cortical function.

title: An impact assessment of a reading and writing instruction method in a socially vulnerable context.
abstract: Educational neuroscience has contributed to a deeper understanding of learning processes by incorporating the sociocultural contexts in which they occur. By using some of the principles that are derived from educational neuroscience, the present study evaluates the impact of an early literacy program in Spanish, the Sophia Method, on preschool and first-grade students from socioeconomically vulnerable backgrounds. The approach adopted integrates the explicit teaching of linguistic, metalinguistic, and graphomotor skills, along with systematic and progressive instruction in reading and writing. A longitudinal quasi-experimental design was employed, featuring an intervention and a comparison group, with two repeated measurements over time. The total sample consisted of 280 Uruguayan students, evenly distributed by sex and drawn from eight schools. The variables assessed are grouped into five dimensions: phonological awareness, alphabetic principle, vocabulary, visomotor skills, and word reading and writing. Mixed-effects linear models and cumulative-link mixed ordinal logistic models showed higher adjusted posttest performance in the intervention condition across all three educational levels. For some outcome variables, the gains made by students participating in the intervention were higher for those starting at lower pretest performance. The findings contribute to the debate on the role of educational neuroscience in the design of culturally situated early literacy practices aimed at effectively improving educational outcomes, with special emphasis on the effective development of early literacy skills in Spanish.

title: From wound to essence: a hypothesis and theory article proposing the Integrative Emotional Alchemy Framework for psychotherapy integration and transformation.
abstract: Contemporary psychotherapy suffers from paradigm fragmentation: affective neuroscience, depth psychology, and evidence-based interventions (EFT, IFS, mindfulness) operate in disciplinary silos without a unifying theory explaining why diverse methods converge on similar therapeutic outcomes. We propose the Integrative Emotional Alchemy Framework (IEAF), a three-stratum theory positing that emotional suffering and transformation operate through nested architecture: (1) Six Wounds of Humanity (Repression, Denial, Shame, Rejection, Guilt, Separation) as ontological core; (2) Eleven Emotion Families as phenomenological middle stratum; and (3) a preliminary taxonomy of Sixty-Four Shadows as behavioural surface patterns. We hypothesise that transformation follows a Shadow→Gift→Essence trajectory, potentially instantiated through reconfiguration of the Default Mode, Executive Control, and Salience Networks, culminating in Fundamental Peace-a dynamic capacity characterised by flexible attentional control, emotional coherence, reduced self-referential rigidity, and compassionate self-awareness. The framework draws on Perceptual Control Theory to provide the functional architecture through which regulation is understood, and synthesises evidence from more than 80 sources across affective neuroscience, psychotherapy research, and contemplative science. A seven-movement clinical protocol (Deconstructive Inquiry Protocol) is introduced alongside preliminary qualitative evidence from semi-structured interviews (N = 24) with community participants in Rajasthan, India-a non-WEIRD population-revealing consistent themes of somatic release, emotional recognition, shadow acceptance, relational shift, meaning reconstruction, and embodied peace. Twelve testable hypotheses with concrete study designs spanning neural mechanisms, mediation pathways, cultural universality, and clinical efficacy provide a clear empirical agenda. The IEAF offers a unified theoretical foundation for psychotherapy integration, a structured protocol applicable across cultural contexts, and a transformation orientation beyond symptom reduction-positioning emotional transformation as an empirically tractable process amenable to rigorous scientific investigation.

title: Effects of orchiectomy on binge-like and inflexible alcohol consumption in mice.
abstract: Alcohol use disorders (AUDs) and excessive alcohol use are a growing public health burden across the world, with sex differences in their presentation. Rodent models of drinking have revealed consistent sex differences in ethanol consumption, preference, and compulsive-like intake. Previous studies have found that ovariectomy reduces ethanol drinking. Increased consumption has also been observed in male, but not female, mice with XY sex chromosome complement. These results and others suggest an interaction between gonadal and genetic sex, but the influence of circulating gonadal hormones has not been assessed. Three experiments used removal of the gonads and the Four Core Genotypes (FCG) mouse line to further investigate interactions between gonadal hormones and sex chromosome complement on alcohol drinking. Experiment 1: ovariectomy (OVX) was conducted before the onset of drinking in XX/Sry- and XY/Sry- FCG females. Experiment 2: orchiectomy (ORX) was performed in C57BL/6J male mice. Experiment 3: ORX was conducted in XX/Sry+ and XY/Sry+ FCG males. Voluntary, binge-like intake of 15% ethanol was measured in a 4-h, two-bottle choice drinking-in-the-dark (DiD) paradigm followed by tests of quinine-resistant drinking (0-500 µM) and, in Experiments 2 and 3 only, ethanol vs. sucrose (1.5-12%) choice. Removal of the testes increased 15% ethanol consumption and preference in male C57BL/6J mice and consumption in FCG mice. Conversely, there was evidence suggesting that ORX reduced quinine-resistance and ethanol vs. sucrose choice in C57BL/6J, but not FCG, males. Previously observed increases in binge-like consumption following OVX were not replicated in FCG female mice. Sex chromosome complement did not interact with gonadal status for any measure. These studies demonstrate that testicular hormones suppress voluntary binge-like ethanol consumption in male mice and provide some evidence for facilitatory effects on two measures of inflexible drinking - quinine resistance and ethanol vs. sucrose choice. These findings are interesting to consider alongside clinical data demonstrating positive associations between testosterone and alcohol drinking in men. There was no evidence for interactions between circulating gonadal hormones and sex chromosome complement, which may suggest gonadal sex-dependent effects of sex chromosome complement on drinking rely on organizational changes earlier in development.

title: Current perspectives: non-rodent models of pain: Pain in Animals Workshop 2025.
abstract: Annually, millions of humans and animals suffer from chronic and acute pain, creating welfare and quality of life concerns for both humans and animals. There is a need to develop new and effective analgesic options as alternatives to opioids and non-steroidal anti-inflammatories (NSAIDs) for humans and animals. A major challenge in developing novel therapeutic approaches is accurately measuring the impact of pain in animal models in a way that is clinically relevant and predictive of clinical efficacy. The Pain in Animals Workshop (PAW) meetings are held every other year in partnership with the National Institutes of Health (NIH), bringing key stakeholders together to improve our understanding of the impact of pain in humans and animals and determine how best to measure this impact. The 2025 workshop explored the following topics: - Current perspectives on non-rodent models, - Artificial intelligence applied to the measurement of pain, - Evolutionary clues to pain mechanisms and novel measures, - Breed and sex differences in pain sensitivity (perceptions and reality). The workshop brought together academic, government, and industry experts. Under the topic of 'Current perspectives on non-rodent models', current views regarding such models were discussed, whilst also showcasing and discussing recent NIH funded/ongoing programs involving these models. With the current interest in non-rodent models and spontaneous disease models, the discussion on successes and challenges was timely. Given the topic's importance and the meeting's uniqueness, this narrative summarizes the presentations and discussions on the topic of current perspectives on spontaneous and other non-rodent disease models.

title: Molecular understanding of liquid-liquid phase separation of α-synuclein for the development of novel Parkinson's disease therapies.
abstract: α-Synuclein (α-syn) exists abundantly at presynaptic terminals and plays a pivotal role in vesicle trafficking and neurotransmitter release thereafter. α-Syn exhibits structural plasticity and adopts diverse conformations such as α-helices and β-strands in response to adjacent microenvironments. These structural features facilitate the formation of aberrant α-syn condensates under specific circumstances. Aggregates and amyloid fibrils of α-syn have been observed in the brain tissue of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and other synucleinopathies. Τhe nucleation of α-syn as a precursor to aggregation and amyloid formation is associated with liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), which forms droplets in solution. Thus, elucidating the detailed molecular formation of α-syn LLPS is necessary to understand the aberrant polymerization of α-syn, such as the formation of amyloid fibrils. In this review, we describe the formation mechanism of α-syn LLPS. In addition, we discuss several molecular strategies for targeting α-syn LLPS to block the formation of α-syn aggregates or amyloid fibrils. This review provides biophysical insights for the development of novel therapies for PD.

title: An integrated computational and experimental framework identifies apigenin as a potential therapeutic agent targeting EGFR/STAT3/MMP9 signaling in glioma.
abstract: Glioma is the most common primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system and is characterized by aggressive progression, high recurrence rates, and limited therapeutic options. Apigenin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits promising anti-tumor properties; however, its molecular mechanisms in glioma remain insufficiently understood. To systematically identify the therapeutic targets and molecular mechanisms underlying apigenin-mediated anti-glioma activity through an integrated computational and experimental approach. An integrated bioinformatics framework combining network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, and machine learning algorithms was applied to identify potential therapeutic targets of apigenin in glioma. Differentially expressed genes were screened using TCGA and GTEx datasets, and prognostic genes were identified through LASSO Cox regression, ElasticNet, and stepwise Cox regression analyses, followed by construction and validation of a multigene prognostic model. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), over-representation analysis (ORA), and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed to explore functional mechanisms. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET prediction were conducted to evaluate the interaction stability and drug-like properties of apigenin with candidate targets. Furthermore, the predicted regulatory axis was examined in LN229 and U87 glioma cell models through cell viability assays, colony formation assays, and Western blotting. Six prognostic genes, including EGFR, MMP9, HIF1A, STAT3, RELA, and CASP3, were identified and used to construct a prognostic model with robust predictive performance. The model achieved favorable discrimination, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC values of 0.840, 0.876, and 0.817, respectively, and a cross-validated C-index of 0.78. Functional enrichment analyses indicated that these genes were primarily associated with cancer-related signaling pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted potential stable interactions between apigenin and key targets, particularly EGFR and STAT3. Cellular experiments showed reduced glioma cell viability following apigenin treatment and reduced colony formation after EGFR or MMP9 knockdown, accompanied by suppression of the EGFR/STAT3 signaling pathway and downstream MMP9 expression. This study established an integrated computational and experimental framework to investigate potential mechanisms associated with the anti-glioma activity of apigenin. Our findings suggest that apigenin-associated growth inhibition in glioma cells involves changes in EGFR/STAT3 signaling and MMP9 expression, providing new insights into its therapeutic potential and supporting further pre-clinical investigation of apigenin as a potential candidate for glioma treatment based on computational and in vitro cellular evidence.

title: Hypertension and risk of dementia subtypes: a Mendelian randomization study in the UK Biobank.
abstract: Hypertension is a modifiable risk factor for dementia. However, the evidence remains inconsistent. We conducted subtype specific analyses by examining the relationships between systolic blood pressure (SBP) and Alzheimer's disease (AD), vascular dementia (VaD) and all-cause dementia (ACD) using observational and individual-level Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses. Observational and MR analyses using logistic and Cox models were used to assess the association between SBP and AD, VaD and ACD. Observational analyses indicated SBP was associated with increased risk of all dementia outcomes. MR analyses indicated genetically proxied SBP was associated with increased risk of all-cause dementia. When stratified by subtype, genetically proxied SBP was associated with increased risk of VaD (Odds Ratio=1.56, [95% CI:1.25;1.93]; Hazards Ratio= 1.58, [95% CI:1.28;1.97]), but not AD (Odds Ratio =1.10, [95% CI:0.95;1.26]; Hazards Ratio=1.11, [95% CI:0.97;1.28]). Hypertension may be more strongly associated with VaD than AD. This highlights the importance of understanding the differential impact of risk factors on different dementia subtypes.

title: Hybridization chain reaction variants with enhanced sensitivity for detecting challenging mRNA targets.
abstract: Compared to traditional enzyme-based in situ amplification methods, Hybridization Chain Reaction v3.0 (HCR v3.0) offers high specificity for spatial RNA visualization but lacks the sensitivity required to robustly detect short or low-abundance targets, particularly in thick tissue with high autofluorescence. Here, we describe three HCR variants that combine the specificity of HCR v3.0 with additional signal amplification through catalytic reporter deposition (HCR-Cat), immunostaining (HCR-Immuno), or iterative HCR and immunodetection (HCR-Multi). These methods substantially enhance detection sensitivity, enabling robust spatial visualization of low-abundance transcripts, improved performance in challenging tissue environments, and compatibility with fluorescence- and alkaline phosphatase-based chromogenic detection. These methods enable transcript-resolution imaging, even when using a limited number of probes, thereby expanding the range of biological applications accessible to HCR.

title: Chronically Implantable Low-Loss Soft Waveguides for Optogenetic Seizure Suppression in Rodents.
abstract: Optical neuromodulation is a promising approach for next-generation therapies targeting neurological disorders. However, clinical translation requires efficient and safe delivery of light to deep brain regions. Conventional solutions used in preclinical studies rely on implantable silica fibers or implantable light sources; however, such stiff implants may exacerbate foreign body responses or generate heat. In contrast, using soft and flexible materials improves tissue compliance but often compromises optical performance and require shuttles or bioresorbable coatings for implantation. To overcome these limitations, a waveguide-based neural probe was developed, fabricated from highly transparent, microfabrication-compatible materials balancing optical efficiency with mechanical compliance. The multimode waveguides exhibit propagation losses below 0.30 dB cm - 1 between λ = 450 and 700 nm, while single-mode waveguides show losses of 0.37-0.41 dB cm - 1 across λ = 488-638 nm. Fabricated from materials with a Young's modulus of approximately 1 GPa, the waveguides provide sufficient stiffness for insertion while maintaining flexibility. Mechanical properties, stability, and implantability were evaluated ex vivo and in vivo in rodents. Biocompatibility was confirmed according to ISO 10993 standards. The waveguides were successfully implanted, and tissue response was assessed using immunohistochemistry after implantation in rats for 6 weeks. Finally, successful optogenetic suppression of experimental seizures was obtained in rats.

title: Longitudinal trajectories of plasma biomarkers, amyloid-β burden and cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Plasma p-tau217 biomarkers support Alzheimer's diagnosis but most evidence remains cross-sectional. Understanding how these biomarkers change over time, whether assays perform similarly, and how such changes relate to Aβ plaque accumulation and cognitive decline is needed to guide patient care. We analyzed 393 cognitively unimpaired and impaired participants from the ADNI-FNIH consortium (mean age 72.7 years; 49% female; 37% Aβ-PET positive) with longitudinal plasma biomarkers across 14 assays, Aβ-PET and cognitive assessments over a mean follow-up of 5.4 years. Plasma p-tau217 was measured across five assays, and Aβ42/40, p-tau181, GFAP and NfL were examined in secondary analyses. Linear mixed-effects models estimated individual rates of change for plasma biomarkers, Aβ-PET Centiloids, and cognitive performance. Linear regressions related concurrent rates of change in plasma biomarkers, Centiloids and cognition in the whole group, by Aβ-PET status, and by Aβ and tau (AT) PET status in a subsample of 272 participants. For comparison, analogous cross-sectional analyses examined associations between plasma biomarker levels and baseline Centiloids or cognitive performance. Finally, semipartial R² values were calculated across all models to quantify the relative variance explained by plasma biomarker and other covariates. Plasma p-tau217 levels increased across all five assays (standardized β = 0.06-0.08, P < 0.001), whereas Aβ42/40 was largely stable. Among Aβ-PET negative individuals, greater p-tau217 increases were consistently associated with concurrent Aβ accumulation (standardized β = 0.40-0.52, P < 0.001), but not in Aβ-PET positive individuals. Conversely, greater p-tau217 increases were most strongly associated with cognitive decline in Aβ-PET positive individuals (standardized β = 0.41-0.56, P < 0.001). In the tau-PET subsample, p-tau217 change was associated with Aβ accumulation in A-T- and, to a lesser extent, A+T- individuals, but not in A+T+ individuals. P-tau217 was the largest contributor to Aβ-PET variance in longitudinal (20.9-28.8%) and cross-sectional (31.8-47.9%) models. For cognition, however, p-tau217 change was the largest contributor in longitudinal models (22.2-30.6%), whereas cognitive status contributed more than p-tau217 cross-sectionally. Although of lower magnitude than for p-tau217, rates of change in p-tau181 and GFAP showed similar stage-dependent associations. In earlier stages, longitudinal changes in p-tau217 paralleled ongoing Aβ accumulation, whereas once Aβ pathology was established, p-tau217 change was more closely associated with cognitive decline than with further Aβ accumulation. These findings indicate that p-tau217 reflects an early Aβ-associated tau response before aggregated tau pathology, supporting the value of longitudinal p-tau217 for stage-dependent disease monitoring.

title: Genotype and Phenotype Correlations in PDCD10 (CCM3) Related Cerebral Cavernous Malformations: A Systematic Review of Clinical, Radiological, and Molecular Evidence.
journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
abstract: Introduction Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) are angiographically occult vascular anomalies. Familial CCM is caused by loss-of-function variants in KRIT1, CCM2, or PDCD10 (CCM3), with PDCD10 deficiency associated with an early and aggressive multisystem phenotype. We synthesized evidence comparing CCM3 with CCM1 and CCM2 and assessed its implications for genotype-informed management. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 and a PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD420261475958), we searched MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science through January 2026 for clinical and experimental studies of PDCD10/CCM3. Study quality was appraised using JBI checklists, NIH tools, and SYRCLE RoB. Results Forty-six studies were included. Compared with CCM1 and CCM2, CCM3 was associated with earlier symptom onset, greater lesion burden, seizures, and intracerebral hemorrhage. Reported extra-CNS manifestations included multiple meningiomas and hematologic cytopenias. Mechanistic studies linked PDCD10 deficiency to disrupted STRIPAK signaling, impaired endothelial-barrier integrity, and altered gut-brain signaling. Conclusions PDCD10-related disease has a severe multisystem phenotype distinct from other familial CCM genotypes. Recognition of its genotype-specific features may inform surveillance, genetic counseling, and therapeutic strategies.

title: Loss of arpin disrupts junction stability and exacerbates inflammation during DSS-induced colitis in mice.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is characterized by chronic mucosal inflammation and disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier. Barrier integrity depends on actin cytoskeletal dynamics that stabilize tight and adherens junctions, a process regulated by the Arp2/3 complex. Whether endogenous Arp2/3 inhibitors control epithelial barrier function during colitis remains unknown. Here, we investigated the role of the endogenous Arp2/3 complex inhibitor arpin in regulating epithelial junction stability and permeability during experimental colitis. Colons from wild-type C57BL/6 mice and CRISPR/Cas9-generated arpin-knockout mice were analyzed under basal conditions and during DSS-induced colitis. Arpin was expressed throughout different colon sections in wild-type mice but absent in knockout mice, without major compensatory changes in proteins related to Arp2/3 complex functions. Arpin deficiency significantly increased basal epithelial permeability. During colitis, arpin expression was reduced in wild-type mice, whereas PICK1 was increased. Although arpin-knockout mice did not develop spontaneous colitis, they exhibited earlier onset and more severe DSS-induced colitis, showing exacerbated crypt loss, edema, leukocyte infiltration, and junctional remodeling marked by increased claudin-2 and reduced E-cadherin and ZO-1 expression and epithelial hyperpermeability. Arpin depletion in colonic epithelial cells recapitulated these defects and enhanced actin stress fiber formation. ROCK1/2 inhibition reduced stress fiber formation and partially restored epithelial electrical resistance, implicating excessive actomyosin contractility in the barrier dysfunction caused by arpin loss. These findings identify arpin as a key cytoskeletal regulator of epithelial barrier integrity and suggest that its loss predisposes the colon to exaggerated barrier failure during inflammation.

title: Emerging Role of m6A Methylation in Atherosclerosis: Mechanisms and Potential Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a severe, life-threatening vascular disease that constitutes the primary pathological basis of acute cardiovascular events. Compared with that in normal tissues, the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification level is dysregulated in atherosclerotic lesion samples. However, the role of m6A modification in the physiological and pathological progression of AS has not been fully elucidated and warrants further in-depth exploration. As a crucial epitranscriptomic modification, m6A methylation is involved predominantly in the posttranscriptional regulation of mRNA translation and metabolism, and is extensively involved in multiple biological and pathological processes. The m6A regulatory system is functionally categorized into writers, erasers, and readers, and the dysregulation of these regulators critically drives atherosclerotic pathogenesis. m6A writers, including METTL3, METTL14, and WTAP, modulate key pathological behaviors of vascular cells during AS progression, including endothelial injury, VSMC phenotypic switching, and macrophage polarization and inflammation. The m6A erasers FTO and ALKBH5 also critically regulate vascular cell dysfunction and atherosclerotic lesion development. In addition, multiple m6A reader families, such as YTHDF/YTHDC, HNRNP, and IGF2BP, participate in the pathological modulation of AS. This review systematically summarizes the regulatory roles of m6A-related factors in RNA alternative splicing during atherosclerotic pathogenesis and discusses their promising potential as novel therapeutic targets for AS intervention. m6A epitranscriptomic modification serves as a core epigenetic mechanism that profoundly modulates atherosclerotic pathogenesis. Accumulating evidence has provided a new avenue for decoding the complex molecular etiology of AS, offering robust mechanistic insights and a solid theoretical basis for developing precise diagnostic biomarkers and targeted therapeutic regimens. Although current advances deepen our understanding of atherosclerotic regulatory networks, further in-depth mechanistic research combined with rigorous clinical validation is still needed to promote the translational application of m6A-based strategies in the precise prevention and treatment of AS.

title: Gratitude as a pathway from childhood emotional maltreatment to hedonic and eudaimonic well-being in young adults: A daily diary study.
abstract: While previous scholarly works have consistently linked childhood emotional maltreatment to reduced well-being, scant evidence has adopted daily diary methods to probe whether emotional maltreatment in childhood is associated with both hedonic and eudaimonic well-being. Furthermore, the underlying mechanisms of this association remain unclear. Therefore, this 14-day daily diary study examined whether childhood emotional maltreatment predicted both hedonic and eudaimonic well-being and tested gratitude as a mediator. Participants included 304 Chinese young adults (249 female; Mage = 19.44 years) who completed baseline measures assessing childhood emotional maltreatment, followed by 14 consecutive daily assessments of hedonic well-being, eudaimonic well-being and gratitude. Multilevel regression analysis demonstrated that childhood emotional maltreatment exerted a negative effect on both facets of well-being, even after controlling for gender, age, socioeconomic status, childhood physical maltreatment, and childhood sexual maltreatment. Furthermore, multilevel mediation analysis indicated that gratitude served as a mediator in the relation between childhood emotional maltreatment and both hedonic and eudaimonic well-being. The current research advances our understanding of the relation between childhood emotional maltreatment and both hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, suggesting that targeted intervention measures can be developed to enhance gratitude and thereby increase well-being.

title: Biocompatible Materials for Electrolyte-Gated Transistors and Neuromorphic Computation.
abstract: The emulation of biological synaptic functions is regarded as the initial step in terms of artificial neural networks and neuromorphic engineering. Electrolyte-gated transistors (EGTs) exploit both ionic and electronic conductivities to present channel-gate capacitance coupling, low operating voltage, large on/off ratio, parallel information processing, and memory functions. By applying biocompatible materials in EGTs, such as chitosan, flexible neuromorphic platform applications can be achieved with lower power consumption and a facile fabrication process. This review introduces EGTs from the history of development, working mechanisms, synaptic plasticity, biocompatible materials used, and advanced applications. EGT-based neuromorphic devices exhibit tremendous advancement and emphasize their significance with regard to neuromorphic engineering and original healthcare technologies in this field. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are discussed. Looking ahead, EGTs are expected to evolve into intelligent bioelectronic systems that integrate sensing, memory, and information processing within a single adaptive material-device platform, paving the way toward bio-inspired physical intelligence and advanced human-machine interfaces.

title: Exosome-like nanoparticles from blueberries modulate hypoxia-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative unbalance in RAW 264.7 cells through the activation of adaptative response.
abstract: Cellular adaptation to hypoxia involves a metabolic shift from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, primarily driven by hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α), often accompanied by increased reactive species (RS) production and oxidative stress. Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) counteracts these effects by regulating antioxidant defences and redox homeostasis. In macrophages, these mechanisms contribute to inflammatory activation and disease progression. Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles (ELNs) have emerged as potential therapeutic agents. This study investigates, for the first time, the protective effects of blueberry-derived ELNs (B-ELNs) against hypoxia-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress in RAW 264.7 macrophages. Hypoxia increased RS production by approximately 150% compared with normoxia. B-ELNs attenuated RS production (approximately 115%), reduced HIF-1α stabilisation (from 2.62- to 1.25-fold), and activated Nrf2 signalling (2.38-fold). These findings suggest that B-ELNs counteract hypoxia-induced metabolic and redox alterations, highlighting their potential as protective bioactive nanostructures against cellular stress.

title: From heterogeneous to identical burst suppression: a continuum of network simplification.
Advanced Microstructural MRI and Clinical Characterization of Paramagnetic Rim Lesion Heterogeneity in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs) reflect chronic active lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS), but their microstructural heterogeneity remains unclear. We characterized quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (qMRI) abnormalities within PRLs, identified data-driven PRL profiles, and examined their associations with disability, brain volumetry, and serum biomarkers. In this longitudinal study, 175 people with MS (pwMS) and 105 healthy controls underwent multiparametric qMRI. Clinical/serum follow-up was available for 113 pwMS (median, 4.4 years). Lesional/perilesional qMRI metrics were derived. Principal component analysis (PCA) characterized PRL heterogeneity, and clustering identified PRL profiles. Mixed-effects models assessed associations with disability, brain parenchymal fraction (BPF), serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (sGFAP). Longitudinal and retrospective MRI assessed 2-year cluster stability and the presence of corresponding lesions 3 years earlier, respectively. PRLs showed greater lesional and perilesional microstructural abnormalities than non-PRLs. PCA identified a dominant continuous damage dimension, along which clustering identified 2 reproducible low- and high-damage profiles. High-damage PRLs were associated with higher disability (β = 0.43; p = 0.035) and lower BPF (β = -0.25; p = 0.002), whereas low-damage PRLs were associated with higher sNfL (β = 0.35; p = 0.010). Longitudinally, low-damage PRLs were associated with steeper increases in disability (βinteraction = 0.12; p = 0.023) and sGFAP (βinteraction = 0.19; p = 0.030), and less favorable microstructural trajectories. Cluster assignments were largely stable longitudinally, and similar proportions of lesions from both clusters were already present 3 years earlier. PRLs exhibit clinically meaningful heterogeneity along a continuous damage spectrum, with cluster assignments largely stable longitudinally. High-damage PRLs are associated with established neurodegeneration, whereas low-damage PRLs show features of ongoing biological activity and worse clinical evolution, supporting the relevance of PRL heterogeneity for prognostic stratification. ANN NEUROL 2026.

title: Skin manifestations and prescribing patterns in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: a multinational study.
journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
abstract: To describe the clinical characteristics and treatments of women with PMOS-related skin concerns presenting to specialist clinics internationally and within the United Kingdom (UK). This retrospective observational study included women with suspected or confirmed PMOS attending eight specialist centers across five countries between January 2020 and December 2023. No lower age limit was specified; all participants were aged ≥16 years. Clinical records provided data on dermatological manifestations and treatments, including doses and formulations, before and after specialist consultation. Of 1313 participants, 1041 (79.3%) had at least one dermatological manifestation; among these, 90.1% had hirsutism, 36.4% had acne, and 6.6% had specialist dermatological review. Metformin and progesterone-only pill predominated in the first and second medication records overall, respectively; in the UK, these were metformin and spironolactone. Prescribing varied significantly across countries and between UK centers. Hirsutism predominated across age groups. In the first medication record, metformin predominated except at ages 16-24, when the combined oral contraceptive pill predominated. Where documented, the most common doses were metformin 1000 mg/day and spironolactone 100 mg/day. Ethnicity closely aligned with recruitment country, limiting interpretation of ethnic differences. Substantial variation exists in pharmacological prescribing patterns across countries and within the UK. Further research is needed to explain these differences and assess their implications for treatment outcomes.

title: Effects of a commercially available sugar-free energy drink on hitting exit velocity in experienced baseball and softball players: a randomized crossover trial.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Caffeine is commonly used as an ergogenic aid, with effective doses often reported at approximately 3-9 mg/kg; however, lower doses are also frequently included in multi-ingredient pre-workout supplements, and the effects of these supplements on sport-specific hitting performance in baseball and softball players remain largely unexplored. Thus, we investigated the acute effects of a commercially available, multi-ingredient caffeinated energy drink (ED) on hitting exit velocity, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, barbell velocity, reaction time, perceived energy, and post-running metabolic outcomes in experienced baseball and softball players. Twenty-two experienced baseball and softball players (14 males, 8 females; mean playing experience: 13 ± 2 years) completed this double-blind, randomized, crossover study. Participants consumed either a sugar-free and caffeinated ED (C4 Performance Energy®; 5 kcal, 200 mg caffeine, β-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and vitamin B12) or a low-calorie, flavor-matched placebo (PLA) during two experimental sessions separated by ≥ 5 days. Testing batteries were performed at three within-session timepoints (T0: pre-consumption; T1: 30 minutes post-consumption; T2: post-exercise) and included CMJs, 30 back squat repetitions at 30% of estimated 1RM, a computerized reaction time test, and subjective perceptual questionnaires. Participants also performed 40 tee hits after T1 and before a high-intensity interval treadmill protocol, followed by 15-minute post-exercise indirect calorimetry. Both average (ED: 71.3 ± 14.0 mph vs. PLA: 70.1 ± 13.5 mph; mean difference ± SD: 1.20 ± 1.41 mph, 95% CI: 0.56-1.84, p < 0.001, dz = 0.85) and peak (ED: 76.7 ± 13.9 mph vs. PLA: 75.1 ± 13.6 mph; mean difference ± SD: 1.56 ± 1.70 mph, 95% CI: 0.79-2.33, p < 0.001, dz = 0.92) hitting exit velocity were significantly greater in the ED condition. A significant condition × time interaction was observed for CMJ height (p = 0.003), whereby jump height was maintained with the ED condition but decreased with PLA at T1. Post-exercise recovery energy expenditure was significantly greater with ED (~5%; p = 0.040, d = 0.46). No significant interactions were observed for barbell velocity, reaction time, or subjective perceptual questionnaires. Acute consumption of a caffeinated multi-ingredient energy drink resulted in small increases in average and peak hitting exit velocity and attenuated transient decline in CMJ height observed with placebo. These findings warrant future investigations with live-pitching conditions in prolonged game simulation settings.

title: Best Possible Self Based Future Specificity Training Enhances Episodic Future Thinking in Individuals With High Schizotypal Traits: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Impaired episodic future thinking (EFT) in individuals with high schizotypal traits (HST) is characterized by reduced specificity and diminished affective engagement in mental simulations. While future specificity training (FeST) improves EFT, integrating personal goal systems through the best possible self (BPS) framework may further enhance intervention effectiveness by strengthening motivational processes. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of a combined BPS and FeST intervention (BPSFST) on EFT in HST and to assess whether effects could be maintained after 3 months. In this preregistered trial, 84 individuals with HST were randomly assigned to either the intervention or control group. The intervention group participated in the BPSFST program for 4 weeks, while the control group was placed on a waitlist. Both groups completed the personal goal EFT task and self-reported measures at baseline, post-intervention and 3-month follow-up. Due to COVID-19 restrictions, the intervention was delivered online, and all assessments were conducted remotely. The intervention significantly improved overall EFT specificity (F(2,402.27) = 23.58, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.10), vividness (F(2,288.28) = 5.60, p = 0.004, ηp 2 = 0.04), sense of experience (F(2,309.73) = 4.91, p = 0.008, ηp 2 = 0.04) and scene details (F(2,302.44) = 7.23, p = 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.05) in individuals with HST, and these improvements were maintained at the 3-month follow-up. The BPSFST intervention enhanced several aspects of EFT in individuals with HST, with effects lasting for 3 months. These findings support the modifiability of EFT in this subclinical population. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2200057524.

title: Causal Computational Modeling of Interpersonal Autonomic Synchrony Reveals the Bidirectional Influence of Dyadic Emotional Co-Regulation During Stress.
abstract: Interpersonal physiological synchrony (IPS) is a promising field of investigation for understanding complex inter-individual processes involved with behavioral and emotional co-regulation. Nonetheless, advancement in this area has been halted by the lack of a robust framework for a precise quantification of IPS, with the majority of research relying on model-free correlational approaches lacking the theoretical and computational foundations necessary to capture the bidirectional and causal nature of these interactions. This study introduces a novel, physiologically-grounded computational model based on coupled integral pulse frequency modulation model and Granger-causality-based estimates to quantify time-resolved, directional autonomic interactions between subjects. The model was validated using a dyadic version of the Trier Social Stress Test (TSST), involving 141 dyads where one participant was actively involved in the stress task (target) and the other participant (observer) sat next to them acting as a source of passive support. Results show that significant synchronization occurs primarily within the parasympathetic component of autonomic nervous system activity. During acute stress, the directional coupling strength from the Target to the Observer (IPSTRG → OBS) decreased, reflecting the target's physiological recruitment and allostatic upregulation to cope with the stressor. Conversely, the coupling strength from the Observer to the Target (IPSOBS → TRG) increased, suggesting that emotional contagion and the Observer's vicarious arousal may drive the dyadic system toward a state of efficient co-regulation. Exploratory analyses further revealed that individual differences in trait empathy, specifically personal distress, differentially moderate these dynamics based on relationship type. In romantic couples, low personal distress in the Observer fostered co-regulation, whereas in strangers, higher personal distress facilitated synchronization. In conclusion, this new computational framework provides a robust tool for quantifying bidirectional physiological synchrony and offers mechanistic insights into how social relationships promote emotional co-regulation and allostatic balance during stress.

title: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Japanese Encephalitis Virus Infection in Mammals.
abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus and the leading cause of viral encephalitis in many regions of Asia. Owing to its pronounced neurotropism, JEV infection can result in severe neurological disease with high mortality, while 30-50% of survivors develop permanent neurological sequelae. Although substantial progress has been made over the past few decades, the molecular mechanisms underlying JEV infection, neuroinvasion, and host-mediated pathogenesis remain incompletely understood. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the understanding of JEV pathogenesis from both viral and host perspectives. We discuss the key events during JEV infection in mammalian hosts, including viral attachment and entry, replication and dissemination, viral determinants of virulence, blood-brain barrier penetration, and the mechanisms underlying central and peripheral nervous system injury. We further compare currently available experimental models for JEV research, including mouse models, porcine models, and human brain organoid systems, highlighting their respective applications, advantages, and limitations in investigating JEV pathogenesis. Collectively, this review provides an integrated overview of the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing JEV infection and neuropathogenesis, identifies current knowledge gaps, and discusses future research priorities that may facilitate the development of effective antiviral and neuroprotective strategies against Japanese encephalitis.

title: From Systemic Infection to Central Nervous System Pathology: Virus-Induced Neuroinflammatory Cascades and Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption.
abstract: Viral infections are recognized triggers of neurological disease through immune-mediated mechanisms that induce acute and chronic neuroinflammation. Although the central nervous system (CNS) is protected by the blood-brain barrier (BBB), several pathogens can access the CNS through mechanisms including leukocyte-mediated "Trojan Horse" entry, endothelial transcytosis, and neuronal transport. Neuropathology frequently seems to be primarily caused by dysregulated host immune responses that activate glial cells and compromise the integrity of the blood-brain barrier. This mini-review summarizes current evidence linking BBB dysfunction to sustained neuroinflammatory cascades, emphasizing microglia-astrocyte interactions and downstream neuronal injury, including synaptic dysfunction and neurodegenerative changes. Using Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as representative examples, we discuss mechanisms of CNS entry, BBB disruption, microglial activation, astrocyte dysfunction, and excitotoxic neuronal injury. We further examine factors governing the transition from protective immune responses to persistent neuroinflammation, including viral latency, chronic immune activation, and microglial priming. Finally, we highlight recent advances in systems biology and systems bioinformatics that enable integration of multi-omics and network-level data to identify conserved pathways underlying virus-associated neurological disease and post-viral syndromes. BBB disruption represents a critical interface linking viral infection to CNS pathology. Convergent inflammatory mechanisms involving glial activation and impaired neurological and immune regulation contribute to persistent neurological dysfunction across diverse viral infections. Integrative systems-level approaches can assist in investigating these mechanisms, while they may also facilitate the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets capable of distinguishing resolving from persistent neuroinflammatory states.

title: Molecularly Aged Protein States as Targets for Drug Design and Delivery in Neurodegenerative Diseases.
abstract: Neurodegenerative drug discovery usually represents a protein target by its gene, canonical sequence, and one or a few structures. That representation can miss the molecular history accumulated by proteins that persist in the brain. Spontaneous chemistry, incomplete repair, altered turnover, proteolysis, phase transitions, and assembly remodeling generate states that may differ from the canonical target in exposure, function, and therapeutic accessibility. We call compositionally resolved species age-generated proteoforms and use molecularly aged protein states when the exact composition remains uncertain. This Review develops a target-state framework for Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia, Huntington disease, and multiple sclerosis. It separates detection from age association, causality, brain exposure, proximal target engagement, and clinical evidence. Disease-specific analyses connect tau and amyloid-beta proteoforms, alpha-synuclein and lysosomal or mitochondrial assemblies, TDP-43 loss-of-function states, and persistent myelin or extracellular-matrix states to rational modalities and critical validation experiments. Repair, selective removal, stabilization, state-selective antibodies and small molecules, intrabodies, replacement, and synthesis control are evaluated together with blood-brain barrier transport, cellular and organelle access, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics. Each class of target state is mapped to the delivery constraint it imposes and the platform for which a precedent exists, and the exposure requirements that state selectivity implies are set out explicitly, including the fraction of a pool that must be engaged, the duration required to move a slowly accumulating state, and the consequences for dosing interval and pharmacodynamic biomarker choice. The aggregate-directed amyloid antibodies are analysed as the existing clinical test of the framework and of its limits. Machine learning remains central to proteoform identification, multimodal prioritization, structure modeling, and molecular design, provided that labels and prospective tests preserve target-state identity. Classical quantum chemistry can address bounded reaction and recognition problems. Quantum computing is treated as an exploratory implementation that requires matched classical baselines and explicit resources. The central requirement is not that an old protein be abnormal, but that a defined disease-relevant state can be selectively engaged while preserving the functional pool.

title: Highways to the Brain: Nanoformulations for the Treatment of Central Nervous System Pathologies.
abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) disorders remain difficult to treat because many pharmacologically active molecules do not achieve adequate exposure in the brain. The blood-brain barrier (BBB), blood-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) barrier, efflux transporters, extracellular matrix, and local clearance mechanisms impose different constraints according to the target compartment and administration route. Nanocarriers can protect unstable payloads, alter pharmacokinetics, and support receptor-mediated or local delivery, but the same properties that promote transport can also increase immune recognition, tissue retention, and neurotoxicity. This review critically examines how nanoparticles (NPs) size, surface charge, composition, degradability, ligand density, and release kinetics should be matched to intravenous, intranasal, intrathecal, intracranial, and oral administration. Rather than treating these routes as interchangeable, we compare the barriers encountered by each route, the payloads for which it is best suited, and the experimental conditions that limit interpretation of reported brain uptake. Particular attention is given to the weak correspondence between many rodent efficacy studies and human delivery constraints, including protein-corona formation after systemic dosing, species differences in BBB and nasal anatomy, limited parenchymal penetration from cerebrospinal fluid, and the procedural risks of direct administration. The resulting route-specific framework is intended to support application-driven formulation design and more informative preclinical evaluation of CNS nanomedicines.

title: Shape as an Independent Design Parameter for Blood-Brain Barrier Crossing: Anisotropic Nanoparticles in Neurodegenerative Diseases.
abstract: Background: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) impose a growing burden, yet effective therapy remains limited because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts CNS drug delivery. Existing reviews treat particle geometry as secondary to composition, size, and surface functionalization. Objectives: This review examines shape anisotropy as an independent design parameter for BBB crossing, arguing that non-spherical geometry qualitatively changes the logic of particle-barrier interaction. Methods: As a narrative review, it synthesizes studies comparing anisotropic and spherical particles of comparable size and surface chemistry, with emphasis on mechanistic evidence linking geometry to transport. Findings: Geometry governs adhesion under flow, membrane wrapping, endocytic route multiplicity, and intracellular trafficking. A barrier-crossing versus penetration-depth trade-off is identified: efficient transcytosis and deep parenchymal distribution are mutually exclusive. The same anisotropy that enhances BBB interaction also reduces its predictability-the "paradox of shape"-owing to the protein corona, endothelial heterogeneity, and disease-altered barrier status. Conclusions: Shape is not a universal "key to the BBB" but a controllable, context-dependent parameter, shifting the field from an optimal geometry toward disease-oriented, robustness-based design.

title: Multi-Task Learning of Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability and hERG Cardiotoxicity: A Random- and Scaffold-Split Evaluation on Experimental Data.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and cardiac hERG liability share physicochemical determinants, motivating the hypothesis that multi-task learning could improve BBB prediction. Methods: We tested this hypothesis using B3DB logBB regression (n = 1058) and a curated hERG dataset (n = 8960). A shared-encoder multi-task neural network was compared with a matched single-task network and Bayesian-optimized gradient boosting under ten random splits, 30 Murcko scaffold splits, and held-out classification sets. Results: Multi-task learning did not improve random-split R2 (0.485 ± 0.016 vs. 0.482 ± 0.015). Under scaffold splitting, its mean R2 was higher (-0.054 vs. -0.817) only because its failures were less severe (the same number of partitions had negative R2); medians were nearly identical (0.394 vs. 0.398). Neither loss weighting, network tuning, nor removal of 39.6% of test compounds sharing a parent structure with hERG training data changed this.
