Gradient boosting was more robust (scaffold R2 = 0.388 ± 0.188; better in 28-29 of 30 partitions), although not significantly so under a dependence-corrected test. Conclusions: Network failures occurred only when a scaffold group containing 18 atypical compounds (e.g., xenon) entered the test set; after removing 20 such compounds, multi-task R2 (0.409) matched gradient boosting (0.420). On 3031 held-out parent structures, AUCs were similar (0.764-0.772).

title: Graph Neural Networks Versus Descriptor-Based Machine Learning for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction: A Matched-Split Evaluation.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability from structure remains challenging. We evaluated whether graph neural networks (GNNs) improve experimental logBB prediction over descriptor-based machine learning and whether GNN attention agrees with earlier descriptor-based findings. Methods: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and Graph Attention Network (GAT) models were trained on 1058 B3DB compounds and compared with LightGBM using 209 RDKit 2D descriptors under identical random and Murcko scaffold splits. Analyses comprised a primary split, 10 repeated random and scaffold splits with nested hyperparameter optimization and paired tests, descriptor-augmented GNNs, classification, external evaluation on the Martins benchmark, and GAT attention analysis. Results and Discussion: In the primary split, LightGBM achieved the highest R2 (random 0.673; scaffold 0.604) versus GCN (0.514; 0.133) and GAT (0.430; 0.310). Across repeated splits with nested hyperparameter optimization, LightGBM outperformed both GNNs under both protocols (paired t-test p < 0.001). GCN and GAT did not differ significantly under scaffold splitting in either the original repeated-split evaluation (p = 0.49) or the optimized comparison (p = 0.184). Descriptor augmentation improved both GNNs (p < 0.001); under scaffold splitting, augmented GCN (R2 = 0.463 ± 0.084) was not significantly different from LightGBM (0.494 ± 0.093; p = 0.22). Using thresholded regression predictions, LightGBM had the highest mean AUC in every condition (≈0.87 versus 0.77-0.84). On 1627 compounds from the independently curated Martins benchmark, mean AUC was 0.84 (LightGBM), 0.83 (GCN) and 0.81 (GAT). GAT attention was higher on nitrogen/oxygen than carbon in 82 of 98 eligible molecules, but halogen, sulfur, and phosphorus atoms received even more attention. Conclusions: Under the evaluated conditions, 2D descriptors outperformed basic GCN and GAT models across splits; descriptor augmentation substantially narrowed the gap. GAT attention provides hypothesis-generating, not causal, insight.

title: Brain Drug Delivery for Major Depressive Disorder and Treatment-Resistant Depression: From Brain Exposure to Clinical Translation.
abstract: The treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) and treatment-resistant depression (TRD) remains challenging because of delayed treatment onset, tolerability concerns, and the need for long-term management. Intranasal administration, molecular optimization, nanocarriers, blood-brain barrier (BBB)-targeted transport, and controlled drug release offer different approaches to improving antidepressant delivery. However, increased drug concentrations in the brain do not necessarily lead to better pharmacological effects; their value depends on whether the drug reaches its site of action and engages the relevant target. This review discusses the mechanisms, brain exposure, pharmacodynamic evidence, and clinical translation of different delivery strategies. Particular attention is given to the interpretive limitations of pharmacokinetic metrics and to the differences in evidence linking carrier distribution, functional cargo delivery, and antidepressant efficacy. Current clinical evidence is concentrated mainly on drugs that have entered clinical use, such as esketamine, whereas most novel targeted carriers and engineered extracellular vesicles remain at the preclinical stage. Their development requires identification of the specific drug-development bottleneck that each delivery system is intended to address, followed by validation of the relationships among effective brain exposure, pharmacological activity, safety, and formulation quality. An evaluation framework matched to the delivery mechanism may help determine whether delivery advantages observed experimentally can translate into meaningful therapeutic benefits.

title: Targeting α7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a severe disorder that is characterized by intrusive thoughts, impaired mood and cognition, hyperarousal, and avoidance in the months and years following a traumatic event. PTSD is comorbid with depression, anxiety, substance abuse, and is challenging for the treatment with psycho- and pharmacotherapy. In light of novel neurobiological findings on the pathogenesis of the disease, innovative approaches to its treatment are investigated. Recently, targeting cholinergic signaling with an antagonist of α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChR), BNC-210, showed a significant promise in clinical trials. This opened up a novel therapeutic strategy that, considering its translational success, calls for a mechanistic understanding. In this review, we dissect the neurobiological role of α7 nAChR in regard of PTSD, and related depression and anxiety states. We discuss the synaptic role of the receptor in fear circuits, immune and endocrine role via the anti-inflammatory cholinergic pathway, and current evidence for the utility of pharmacological modulation of α7 nAChR.

title: Ligand-Engineered Nanoplatforms for Receptor-Mediated Drug Delivery Across the Blood-Brain Barrier: Design Principles and Translational Considerations.
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) excludes most therapeutic agents from the central nervous system and remains a major constraint in the treatment of glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and other neurological disorders. Receptor-mediated transcytosis (RMT) offers a non-invasive route in which ligand-functionalized carriers engage receptors on brain endothelial cells and undergo vesicular transport across the BBB. This review examines transferrin (Tf), apolipoprotein E (ApoE), and receptor-binding peptides as the principal ligand classes used to engineer BBB-penetrating nanoplatforms, including polymeric nanoparticles, liposomes, micelles, lipid nanoparticles, and biomimetic carriers. Unlike reviews organized primarily by carrier type, administration route, or disease indication, we use a ligand-centered framework to connect receptor selection with affinity and avidity, surface density and orientation, intracellular trafficking, and carrier architecture. Particular attention is given to the progression from full-length natural proteins to compact peptides and stability-engineered ligands, including retro-inverso, stapled, and stimulus-cleavable designs. We also summarize representative within-study improvements in brain delivery and therapeutic outcome while emphasizing that effect sizes depend on the BBB model, disease model, dosing regimen, comparator, and analytical endpoint. Finally, we discuss species specificity, receptor-mediated safety liabilities, conjugation reproducibility, scale-up, and human-relevant BBB evaluation. These considerations position ligand engineering and pharmaceutical manufacturability as interdependent requirements for translating RMT nanoplatforms into clinically viable CNS drug-delivery systems.

title: From Passive Carriers to Niche Engineers: The Evolving Paradigm of Engineered Bacteria in Cancer Therapy.
abstract: Engineered bacterial systems have been predominantly conceptualized as living drug-delivery vehicles, with their therapeutic value attributed primarily to tumor-homing capabilities and payload delivery. This framing, while productive in guiding early-stage research, may inadvertently constrain both the design space and the therapeutic ambition of bacterial therapeutics. An alternative perspective is emerging from recent advances in synthetic biology and tumor immunology: bacteria may be understood not merely as passive carriers of therapeutic payloads but as active participants in the remodeling of the tumor ecosystem. This review examines the conceptual and empirical foundations of this paradigm shift, tracing the evolution from bacteria as delivery vehicles to bacteria as "niche engineers" capable of metabolic reprogramming, immunological modulation, and structural reorganization of the tumor microenvironment. The discussion progresses through four interconnected dimensions-colonization, remodeling, orchestration, and adaptation-each of which redefines the bacterium's functional role in the therapeutic context. Critically, the review engages with unresolved mechanistic questions that complicate the therapeutic narrative, including the dual role of IL-10 in both sustaining bacterial persistence and suppressing antitumor immunity, the spatial heterogeneity of bacterial colonization and its implications for therapeutic efficacy, and the evolutionary pressures that may select for loss-of-function mutants. The clinical translation landscape is examined with attention to manufacturing challenges, regulatory uncertainties, and the potential failure modes of combination strategies. By situating engineered bacteria within the broader ecological dynamics of the tumor microenvironment, this review aims to provide a framework for the next generation of bacterial therapeutics that engage more fully with the complexity of cancer as a systemic disease.

title: Recent Advances in Electrospun Nanofiber Membrane Based Biomimetic Tissue Barriers and Drug Screening Functions.
abstract: The construction of highly biomimetic in vitro tissue barrier models is essential for new drug development, as it enables accurate evaluation of the permeability efficiency, safety, and pharmacokinetic properties of drug candidates. Animal models have long been regarded as the standard criterion for assessing drug efficacy; however, they pose increasingly severe ethical concerns. Moreover, substantial interspecies differences in transmembrane transporter expression and metabolic pathways contribute to the low rate of successful clinical translation. Traditional 2D cell culture models lack a 3D matrix microenvironment and physiological mechanical signals similar to those in vivo. Consequently, epithelial or endothelial cells are prone to phenotypic alteration. They struggle to assemble structurally intact and functionally mature tight barriers. As a result, drug permeability and toxicity results often deviate markedly from in vivo physiological conditions. In contrast, electrospinning technology offers a promising approach for constructing biomimetic barriers. Electrospun nanofiber membranes closely resemble the fibrous network structure of the natural extracellular matrix and provide several distinct advantages, including precisely controllable pore sizes, large specific surface areas, and readily modifiable functional surfaces. Furthermore, the arrangement and physicochemical properties of the fibers can be precisely tailored to provide cells with inductive cues that mimic the in vivo physiological microenvironment. This review summarizes the design strategies of electrospun nanofiber membranes for the construction of key tissue barriers, including the lung, blood-brain barrier, intestine, kidney, and skin. In addition, it discusses recent advances in the application of these membranes for drug screening. Finally, universal design principles for cross-barrier construction are proposed. Overall, this review aims to support the development of more efficient and reliable in vitro drug-screening platforms.

title: Isolation and Absolute Configuration Assignment of a New Stemona tuberosa Alkaloid by DFT 13C NMR and Specific Rotation.
abstract: Stemona tuberosa Lour. is a well-known medicinal plant rich in bioactive alkaloids. Stemona-type alkaloids possess intricate polycyclic skeletons with multiple stereogenic centers, which makes full structural and stereochemical characterization challenging, and their bioactivities warrant further investigation. In this work, four compounds, including three alkaloids (1, 2 and 3) and one bibenzyl derivative (4), were isolated from the roots of Stemona tuberosa Lour. Their structures were elucidated using 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy and HR-ESI-MS. Quantum chemical calculations combining 13C NMR chemical shift simulation and specific optical rotation prediction were applied to assign the absolute configurations of the new alkaloid (compound 1) and stemona-amine B (2). All isolates were evaluated for anti-inflammatory, acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory, and cytotoxic activities. Compound 4 displayed potent anti-inflammatory activity with an IC50 of 2.57 ± 0.12 μM, superior to the positive control quercetin (IC50 = 7.07 ± 0.80 μM). Compounds 2 and 3 showed mild AChE inhibitory effects, and none of these compounds displayed cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations.

title: Toxicokinetics, Postmortem Distribution, and Redistribution of Epinephrine and Its Metabolites.
abstract: Epinephrine (Epi) is an endogenous catecholamine, and interpretation of its concentrations in forensic investigations is complicated by rapid metabolism, stress-related release, and postmortem concentration changes. In this study, a liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method was developed to simultaneously determine Epi and its three metabolites, including metanephrine (MN), epinephrine glucuronide (Epi-Glu), and epinephrine-4-O-sulfate (Epi-4-O-S), in rats' biological samples. Following intravenous Epi administration in rats, toxicokinetics, tissue distribution, and postmortem changes were investigated. Epi concentrations increased rapidly after administration and declined toward endogenous levels within 90 to 180 min. MN showed an early maximum, whereas Epi-Glu exhibited a non-monotonic profile with a late increase and remained measurable through 72 h; Epi-4-O-S was not detected in blood during the toxicokinetic experiment. Immediately after death, Epi was abundant in blood, MN was detected across multiple tissues, Epi-Glu was enriched in liver, and Epi-4-O-S was relatively higher in lung and liver. During the postmortem interval (PMI), all analytes showed matrix-dependent changes. Cardiac-to-peripheral blood (C/P) and unit-normalized liver-to-peripheral blood (L/P) indices further demonstrated site-dependent concentration divergence. These findings characterize the toxicokinetic and postmortem behaviors of Epi and its metabolites and provide experimental data for forensic interpretation of suspected Epi exposure.

title: Screening of Antidepressant Active Components from Thymus quinquecostatus and the Underlying Mechanisms Based on Neural Stem Cell and Glial Cell Plasticity.
abstract: This study aimed to screen the active components of Thymus quinquecostatus with antidepressant effects and to explore the underlying mechanisms based on hippocampal neuroplasticity. A chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model of depression was established. The intervention effects of five active components-thyme volatile oil, thymol, carvacrol, p-cymene, and β-caryophyllene (BCP)-were systematically evaluated using behavioral, endocrine, histomorphological, and molecular approaches (50 mg/kg, intraperitoneal injection, once daily for 14 days). All active components significantly reduced serum corticosterone levels (decreased by 27.1-64.7%, p < 0.001) and increased the sucrose preference rate (increased by 39.5-55%, p < 0.05). carvacrol and p-cymene significantly shortened immobility time in the tail suspension test (decreased by 17-20.9%), whereas thymol, BCP, and volatile oil effectively reduced feeding latency in the novelty-suppressed feeding test (decreased by 63.4-67.8%). p-cymene, BCP, and volatile oil significantly increased the number of BrdU+ proliferating cells and DCX+ immature neurons in the hippocampal dentate gyrus (p < 0.05-0.001). All five components increased the number of microglial terminal endpoints by 41-70%, indicating a shift toward a resting/anti-inflammatory phenotype, and some components also restored astrocyte morphology and density (p < 0.05). All five components significantly activated AKT (p-AKT/AKT increases of more than 91%), whereas only volatile oil, carvacrol, and p-cymene significantly activated CREB (p-CREB/CREB increases of 34-50%), suggesting that AKT/CREB signaling participates in the regulation of neuronal survival and plasticity. Collectively, these components ameliorated depression-like behaviors in mice potentially through a multi-target, heterogeneous network-including inhibiting HPA axis overactivation, promoting neurogenesis, inducing glial anti-inflammatory phenotype transformation, and activating AKT/CREB survival signaling-rather than a simple, linear synergistic mechanism. Notably, the pronounced effect of p-cymene on neurogenesis may partly reflect its higher absolute administered dose compared to its natural abundance in the volatile oil. Among them, p-cymene, BCP, carvacrol, and volatile oil displayed promising therapeutic potential. These preliminary findings provide an experimental basis for the development of natural multi-target antidepressants based on neural stem cell-glial cell network regulation.

title: Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction: Machine Learning, Graph Neural Networks, and Protonation-State Robustness.
abstract: Blood-brain barrier permeability (BBBP) prediction is important for central nervous system (CNS) drug discovery, yet the relative performance of traditional molecular feature-based models and graph neural networks (GNNs), as well as the sensitivity of BBBP predictions to molecular protonation states, remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we curated the public OmniBBBP dataset through structural deduplication, label-conflict resolution, and removal of compounds overlapping with an external benchmark, yielding 8836 compounds for model development. Four traditional machine learning (ML) models and three GNN architectures (GCN, GAT, and PNA) were evaluated using repeated similarity-cluster cross-validation (CV). XGBoost combining 173 RDKit descriptors with a 1024-bit Morgan fingerprint achieved the strongest overall performance, with accuracies of 0.893 and 0.860 and Matthews correlation coefficients (MCCs) of 0.765 and 0.720 on the fixed test set and 200-compound external benchmark, respectively. Its benchmark performance was comparable to that reported for the deep learning model BBBP-Atlas, whereas PNA showed complementary performance among compounds with low structural similarity to the training set. To investigate protonation-state sensitivity, benchmark compounds were expanded into 962 protomeric structures, and XGBoost was retrained using a protomer-expanded training set while retaining the same molecular features and hyperparameters. Protomer-expanded training increased benchmark accuracy from 0.830 to 0.850 and MCC from 0.660 to 0.701, indicating improved robustness to alternative protonation-state representations. Overall, these results demonstrate that descriptor- and fingerprint-based XGBoost provides a competitive BBBP classification baseline under the present data and evaluation conditions and that incorporating alternative protomeric representations during training can further improve prediction robustness.

title: Ozone Pretreatment Modulates Chemical and Volatile Profiles During Rhizopus oligosporus Fermentation of Faba Bean.
abstract: Faba bean is a promising substrate for tempeh-like products, although its sensory characteristics and the presence of compounds such as vicine, convicine and L-DOPA may limit its wider use. This study investigated whether ozone pretreatment modifies chemical and aroma-related changes during Rhizopus oligosporus NRRL 2710 fermentation of faba bean. Non-ozonated and ozonated samples were fermented for 15, 22, 39 and 46 h and analysed for free amino acids (FAA), L-DOPA, vicine and convicine by HPLC, while volatile compounds were evaluated by SPME-GC-MS, multivariate analysis and sensory assessment. Ozone pretreatment strongly modified the later stages of fermentation. Total FAA increased to 543.55 mg/100 g DW in O46 samples, compared with 48.20 mg/100 g DW in NO46 samples. L-DOPA decreased mainly as a function of fermentation time, whereas significant time × ozone interactions were observed for vicine and convicine, with markedly lower concentrations in ozonated samples at prolonged fermentation. Volatile profiles also diverged most strongly at 39-46 h, with several grassy/green-associated compounds not detected from late ozonated samples. However, ozonated tempeh evaluated after 24 h showed stronger pungent/ammonia notes and overall aroma. Overall, ozone pretreatment altered fermentation-associated chemical and volatile development in a time- and compound-dependent manner.

title: Racetams: Chemical Structures, Molecular Mechanisms of Action, Neuropharmacology, and Clinical Evidence-A Critical Narrative Review.
abstract: Racetams are structurally related but pharmacologically heterogeneous compounds studied in relation to cognition. This narrative and critical review compares piracetam, aniracetam, oxiracetam, pramiracetam, phenylpiracetam, fasoracetam, and levetiracetam with respect to chemical structure, stereochemistry, proposed mechanisms, clinical evidence, safety, and regulatory status. Literature searches identified historical publications, preclinical studies, clinical trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses relevant to these compounds. The findings indicate that a shared structural scaffold does not imply a common molecular target or equivalent clinical effects. Proposed mechanisms range from membrane-related effects and glutamatergic or cholinergic signaling to dopamine-transporter activity, metabotropic glutamate receptor-associated signaling, and SV2A binding by levetiracetam. Clinical evidence varies by compound, population, and outcome; many cognitive-enhancement claims rely on small or older trials, while several mechanistic observations derive from preclinical models. Animal findings cannot establish clinical neuroprotection, neurogenesis, or cognitive enhancement in humans. Levetiracetam has an established antiseizure indication, which does not establish a nootropic indication. Current evidence does not support class-wide conclusions about efficacy or long-term safety. Generative AI was used to assist with literature discovery and the preparation of schematic figures. All AI-suggested references were independently checked against PubMed records and DOI metadata, and the authors reviewed the AI-assisted material and take full responsibility for the accuracy and integrity of the manuscript. Further well-designed clinical trials and direct pharmacological comparisons are needed.

title: Plant Flavonoids and Polyphenols as Modulators of Biomolecular Condensates: Pharmacological Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: Plant flavonoids and other polyphenols have been investigated for their effects on protein homeostasis, but their role in regulating biomolecular condensates, membraneless compartments formed through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), remains poorly understood. While direct biophysical evidence for polyphenol-mediated LLPS modulation is currently limited to a small number of compounds (notably EGCG, curcumin, and gallic acid) and protein targets (primarily Tau and α-synuclein), indirect evidence suggests that polyphenols may influence condensate biology through oxidative stress modulation, chaperone induction, autophagy activation, and effects on post-translational modifications. This review critically examines the available evidence, applying an explicit classification framework that distinguishes direct biophysical evidence, direct cellular evidence, and indirect mechanistic associations. We provide a comparative structure-activity analysis of representative polyphenols and evaluate the translational gap between in vitro effective concentrations and achievable systemic and brain exposure. Our synthesis indicates that while polyphenols represent promising tool compounds for investigating condensate biology, their therapeutic potential as condensate-modulating agents remains speculative and requires substantially more direct evidence, including validation in disease-relevant models, testing of circulating metabolites, and demonstration of achievable exposure at target sites. Finally, current knowledge gaps and future research directions will be discussed with the aim of clarifying the current stage of preclinical evidence and the substantial work still required before the therapeutic relevance of plant polyphenols as modulators of biomolecular condensate biology can be evaluated.

title: Deep Eutectic Solvents as an Eco-Efficient Alternative for the Sustainable Recovery of Multitarget Alkaloids from Bocconia frutescens.
abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as sustainable alternatives to conventional organic solvents for the extraction of bioactive natural products. This study developed a green extraction strategy for recovering neuroactive alkaloids from Bocconia frutescens roots using DES-based systems. Thirteen DES formulations were evaluated and compared with conventional aqueous and ethanolic extraction. UHPLC-DAD and UHPLC-ESI-HRMS analyses identified sanguinarine and chelerythrine as the major benzophenanthridine alkaloids present in the extracts. Among the solvents tested, a citric acid-glucose (1:1) DES exhibited the highest extraction efficiency. Extraction parameters were optimized using a Box-Behnken response surface design, evaluating the effects of plant material-to-solvent ratio, temperature, and effect of water addition. Under optimized conditions, alkaloid recovery increased four-fold compared with the central experimental point, reaching a maximum alkaloids concentration of 400.1 ppm. The optimized alkaloid-rich extract displayed potential neuroprotective activity, inhibiting acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase with IC50 values of 2.96 and 46.79 μg/mL, respectively. Additionally, the extract strongly inhibited Aβ1-42 aggregation, exhibiting an IC50 value of 0.70 μg/mL. Finally, to assess the greenness of the analytical method here employed, the green analytical procedure index (GAPI) and the analytical greenness metric approach and software (AGREE version 0.5 BETA) were used, and these metrics show that the ecofriendly character is mainly based on factors such as the low sample size, the use of bio-based solvents and the lack of other hazards associated with handling toxic petroleum-derived solvents. These results demonstrate that DES-assisted extraction is an efficient and environmentally sustainable approach for obtaining alkaloid-enriched extracts from B. frutescens and highlight their potential as multitarget agents for Alzheimer's disease management.

title: Cinnamaldehyde-Containing Combinations Demonstrate Favourable Cytotoxicity and Nitric Oxide Inhibitory Profiles In Vitro.
abstract: Skin inflammation is a common dermatological concern that arises from infections. Essential oil compounds (EOCs) have garnered interest due to their potent anti-inflammatory properties. Preliminary studies have shown antimicrobial synergistic interactions between EOCs and conventional antimicrobials. The current study investigated the cytotoxicity and the ability to inhibit LPS-induced nitric oxide production of six EOCs (α-pinene, γ-terpinene, linalool, eugenol, carvacrol, and cinnamaldehyde) in combination with eight conventional antimicrobials using the MTT assay (HaCAT keratinocytes) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. The cytotoxicity of the EOCs on HaCAT keratinocytes was dose-dependent, with IC50 values ranging from 274.0 µg/mL (linalool, least cytotoxic) to 28.6 µg/mL (cinnamaldehyde, most cytotoxic). Among the conventional antimicrobials, only miconazole demonstrated noteworthy toxicity against HaCAT cells. Among the combinations tested, amoxicillin-carvacrol (92.09%) and miconazole-carvacrol (91.82%) demonstrated the highest cell viabilities, while miconazole-cinnamaldehyde (78.53%) and erythromycin-cinnamaldehyde (78.42%) produced the greatest reductions in nitric oxide production. Ciprofloxacin-cinnamaldehyde demonstrated one of the most favourable overall profiles, combining substantial nitric oxide inhibition (77.66%) with the lowest cytotoxicity interaction index (CI = 0.12). All combinations involving cinnamaldehyde were interpreted as synergistic with respect to both reduced cytotoxicity and inhibition of LPS-induced nitric oxide production under the conditions tested. Among the combinations evaluated, ciprofloxacin-cinnamaldehyde demonstrated the most favourable overall profile in the in vitro screening models, with reduced cytotoxicity and inhibition of LPS-induced nitric oxide production. These findings support further investigation of this combination in additional experimental models; however, the present results should be interpreted as preliminary and are not sufficient to establish therapeutic efficacy in skin infections. These findings were obtained using in vitro screening models and require validation in additional skin-relevant cellular and in vivo models before therapeutic relevance can be established.

title: Analytical Methods for the Determination of Diamine Oxidase (DAO) Activity: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Diamine oxidase (DAO) is an extracellular enzyme that plays a key role in the intestinal degradation of exogenous histamine. Given its association with histamine intolerance and its potential applications in food biotechnology and dietary supplements, the accurate determination of DAO activity has become essential in both clinical and food-related contexts. This review provides a comprehensive and critical evaluation of the analytical methods reported for the determination of DAO activity, including spectroscopic, radiometric, immunological, chromatographic, zymographic, mass spectrometric and electrochemical techniques. Their underlying principles, analytical performance, advantages and limitations, and suitability for different sample matrices are compared, distinguishing methods that measure catalytic activity from those that quantify DAO protein concentration. Particular emphasis is placed on the influence of the reaction substrate and assay conditions on the measured activity, and on the need to align substrate selection with the intended application, including the clinical investigation of histamine intolerance and the evaluation of DAO-based dietary supplements. This review offers practical guidance for selecting appropriate methods according to the analytical objective and identifies current challenges and priorities for the standardisation of DAO activity determination.

title: Molecular Dynamics Reveals Persistent Alternative Binding Conformations of a Donepezil-Melatonin Hybrid in Human Butyrylcholinesterase: Implications for Alzheimer's Disease Drug Discovery.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder in which declining acetylcholinesterase activity increases the relative importance of butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) in cholinergic regulation. Compound 4u, a donepezil-melatonin hybrid, was previously reported to inhibit human BChE with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 56 nM. We investigated its BChE-bound dynamics using three independently propagated 200 ns molecular dynamics replicas and a 100 ns simulation of crystallographically bound tacrine, totaling 700 ns. Compound 4u remained within the binding gorge in all three replicas, with persistent critical-residue contacts and replica-dependent hydrogen bonding. Clustering, supported by an alternative distance-based clustering method, revealed two persistent bound-state ensembles with replica-dependent populations: one ensemble accounted for 74.5%, 16.5%, and 100.0% of snapshots sampled at 1 ns intervals from replicas 1-3, respectively. Equilibrium state populations and kinetic metastability were not established. Despite distinct dominant conformations, the replicas produced complete-trajectory molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area (MM/GBSA) estimates (-47.11, -45.66, and -48.66 kcal/mol for replicas 1-3, respectively) and shared a stabilizing core involving Trp82, Leu286, Phe329, and Tyr332. Tacrine retained its crystallographic anchoring environment. These results indicate that compound 4u combines persistent BChE engagement with conformational adaptability, providing testable structural hypotheses for future analogue design and experimental validation.

title: Pharmacovigilance Signal Detection of Vortioxetine in Individuals Aged over 65 Years: A Disproportionality FAERS Analysis Versus Other Antidepressants.
abstract: Background: Recently, vortioxetine has emerged as a potential safe antidepressant alternative in the elderly population. Safety signals of vortioxetine were evaluated against other antidepressants in patients aged over 65. Methods: Data from the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System (FAERS) database were analyzed to identify potential safety signals by analyzing patterns and trends in adverse-event reports in which the drug was listed as the primary suspect, extracted up to February 2025. Report characteristics (sex, outcome, year, country, and indication) were described, and disproportionality analyses were conducted to compare vortioxetine adverse events between age groups (18-65 vs. >65) and versus other antidepressants. Results: Vortioxetine represented the primary-suspect antidepressant with reporting peaking around 2018. Age-stratified disproportionality analyses showed that older adults had disproportionate reporting of neuropsychiatric events, falls/trauma, cardiovascular rhythm disturbances, and electrolyte/metabolic abnormalities vs. younger adults, suggesting increased vulnerability to multisystem adverse outcomes. Compared to other antidepressants (SSRIs, trazodone, mirtazapine, SNRIs, and the TCAs amitriptyline and nortriptyline), the strongest disproportionality signals for vortioxetine were largely driven by mood-related ADRs, medication errors, and respiratory compromise terms. Conclusions: The findings represent pharmacovigilance signals derived from FAERS data and should be considered hypothesis-generating, requiring confirmation through further clinical and epidemiological studies.
